quote: Well, right now, I pay 429 every month.
stewart_read: Strong bill capture early and unprompted by the customer, a good anchor point.
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged the pain but never flipped it into 'that $429 is the actual expense, solar removes it' — see anchor_use.

quote: the government is helping out with, with the solar. I don't know.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers awareness of incentives — a hook the rep could use to build curiosity about her specific numbers.
coaching_implication: Rep could have said something like 'that's exactly what we'll show you on your specific design' instead of pivoting straight into the credit qualifier as a gate.

quote: The only thing that you need to qualify for those programs is that you have a credit score above 670.
stewart_read: Rep applies the 670 threshold rigidly to a self-reported, uncertain number without acknowledging the schema's own note that stated credit often differs from pulled credit.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep followed the DQ rule as scripted, believing self-reported credit is the gate.
coaching_implication: Per qualifiers.credit_qualifier drift/policy note, rep should pass the lead to the closer's actual credit pull rather than DQ on an unconfirmed guess.

stewart_read: This is treated as a hard DQ trigger instead of an opportunity to flip — e.g., 'that's close, let's get you in front of the closer who can check exact numbers.'
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may be following a strict DQ policy — but no schema confirmation exists that self-reported credit is a hard gate over a pulled credit check.
coaching_implication: Rep should have offered a path forward (closer verifies via actual pull) rather than closing the door on a customer's own uncertain guess.

quote: Yeah. So to qualify for those grants and those credits, you do need to have a credit score above 670.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same credit line with no new angle — a restate, not a new attempt.
coaching_implication: Repeating the same fact isn't a new attempt; rep needed an alternative move (financing options, closer routing) here.

quote: So if I were you, I would just give us a callback when your guys' credit is high enough,
stewart_read: Call ends with no locked time, no text follow-up promise, and no specific next step — pure soft exit.
coaching_implication: Even on a DQ, rep should set a concrete follow-up date or hand off to a supervisor/credit-repair resource rather than leaving it open-ended.
